title: cboard2: hookless multi-repo git dashboard
description:
Rebuild changeboard (~/git/changeboard) so it needs no Claude Code hook. changeboard relies on a PostToolUse(Bash|Edit|Write) hook that snapshots git state into a shared SQLite store; only repos an agent touched ever appear. cboard2 derives everything from git and the filesystem instead, so every clone on disk shows up whether or not an agent has been near it.

Design decisions, measured on the author's machine (94 repos in ~/git, 109 under $HOME at depth 4):

- Current state comes from 'git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch' per repo. 0.28s for all 94 repos at 16 worker threads, so a 1-2s poll is affordable. --no-optional-locks matters: it stops the poller taking .git/index.lock and racing the user's own git commands.
- Recent activity comes from the reflog ('.git/logs/HEAD'), which records every HEAD movement with a unix timestamp and a verb: commit, checkout, merge, pull, rebase, reset, clone. This is the retroactive replacement for changeboard's 'events' table and its 'git_verb' column.
- Working-tree edits touch nothing under .git, so the reflog cannot see them. The newest mtime among the paths 'git status' reports as modified or untracked stands in for 'last edited'.
- No SQLite, no collector, no events table. git and the filesystem are the store. That drops store.py (390 lines) and collector.py (498 lines) from the changeboard design. A JSON cache of discovered repo paths avoids rescanning at startup, and is disposable.

What carries over from changeboard: the Textual table (repo, branch, HEAD subject, dirty state, ahead/behind, recency), the dirty/unpushed filters, the sort cycle, the detail screen, and the scripting subcommands (ls, json, busy).

What is dropped: the hook, the collector, the SQLite store, the 'session' column and session filter (there is no session without a hook), 'prune', and 'add'/'forget' as store operations (discovery replaces them; ignore rules replace 'forget').
acceptance: Running 'cboard2' with no arguments opens a dashboard listing every git repo under the configured roots, with no hook installed anywhere. Each row shows live branch, dirty counts and ahead/behind. A commit made in another terminal shows up in the activity view within one poll interval.

title: cboard2: hookless multi-repo git dashboard
Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
description:
cboard2 has no hook, so it cannot learn about repos from agent activity. It finds them by walking the filesystem.

New module: 'src/cboard2/discovery.py'.

Walk each configured root, prune at any directory containing a '.git' entry (do not descend into a repo looking for nested ones), and return the repo roots. Measured cost on the author's machine: 'find ~ -maxdepth 4 -name .git -type d -prune' returns 109 repos in 0.3s, so a plain os.scandir walk with a depth cap is fast enough to run at startup.

Config lives at '$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cboard2/config.toml' (falling back to '~/.config'), read with tomllib from the standard library:

  roots = ["~/git"]
  max_depth = 4
  ignore = ["~/git/_old"]

Defaults when the file is absent: roots = ['~'], max_depth = 4, ignore = []. Expand '~' in every path. An ignore entry matches a repo root exactly or any repo beneath it.

Cache the discovered paths as JSON at '$XDG_CACHE_HOME/cboard2/repos.json' so a restart renders before the walk finishes. The cache is disposable: a missing or corrupt file means rescan, never an error. Prune paths that no longer exist on disk.

Env override 'CBOARD2_CONFIG' points at an alternate config file, for tests.
acceptance: discover() on a tmp_path tree containing two repos, a nested repo inside one of them, and a plain directory returns exactly the two outer repo roots. An ignore entry naming a parent directory excludes every repo under it. A corrupt repos.json triggers a rescan rather than raising. A missing config file yields the documented defaults.

title: Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
description:
The dashboard's live columns (branch, dirty counts, ahead/behind, HEAD subject) come from polling git directly. There is no stored snapshot to read.

New module: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'.

Per repo, one call: 'git --no-optional-locks -C <root> status --porcelain=v2 --branch'. The '--no-optional-locks' flag is not optional here: without it the poller refreshes and rewrites '.git/index', taking 'index.lock' and racing whatever git command the user is running in that repo. git added the flag for exactly this class of status-bar tool.

The porcelain-v2 parser in '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/collector.py' (parse_porcelain_v2, _parse_ab) is correct and worth porting: it reads '# branch.head' (with the '(detached)' case), '# branch.oid' (with '(initial)'), '# branch.upstream', '# branch.ab', then counts staged/unstaged from the XY field of '1 '/'2 ' lines, unmerged from 'u ' lines, untracked from '? ' lines.

HEAD subject and commit time need a second call: 'git -C <root> log -1 --format=%s%x09%ct'. Return None for both when it fails, which is what an empty repo with no HEAD does.

Run the repos through a ThreadPoolExecutor. Measured: 94 repos in 0.28s at 16 workers, versus 1.4s serial. A repo whose git calls fail or time out (5s) is reported as unreadable rather than dropped, so a broken clone stays visible.

Expose a frozen dataclass RepoState carrying: path, name, branch, detached, head_sha, head_subject, head_time, staged, unstaged, untracked, ahead, behind, upstream. No last_touched or last_session fields — recency comes from the activity reader, and there are no sessions without a hook.
acceptance: poll() over a tmp_path repo with a staged file, a modified tracked file and an untracked file reports staged=1, unstaged=1, untracked=1. A detached HEAD sets detached=True and branch=None. A repo with no commits yields head_sha=None and head_subject=None without raising. A non-repo path is reported unreadable, not dropped. Every git invocation the module makes includes --no-optional-locks (assert it in a test that captures the argv).

Read recent activity from each repo's reflog
description:
This replaces changeboard's whole hook-and-events mechanism. changeboard recorded a 'git_verb' per bash command into a SQLite 'events' table; git already keeps that log itself, in the reflog, with better coverage and full history.

New module: 'src/cboard2/activity.py'.

Read HEAD movements with 'git -C <root> reflog --date=unix --format=%gd%x09%ct%x09%gs%x09%h' (verified working). The '%gs' selector carries the verb and its detail, in forms like:

  commit: Add cboard add command
  commit (initial): Initial project setup
  checkout: moving from main to feature-x
  pull --rebase: Fast-forward
  reset: moving to HEAD~1

Parse the leading token up to ':' as the verb, keep the rest as detail, and normalise 'commit (initial)' and 'commit (amend)' to 'commit'. Timestamps are unix seconds from '%ct'.

Two more cheap sources belong here:

- Per-branch recency, one call: 'git -C <root> for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate refs/heads --format=%(refname:short)|%(committerdate:unix)|%(subject)'. Feeds the detail view.
- Last fetch: the mtime of '.git/FETCH_HEAD'. There is no reflog entry for a fetch that moved nothing.

Reading the reflog for 100 repos on every poll is wasteful. Gate it on the mtime of '.git/logs/HEAD': re-read a repo only when that mtime has moved since the last read. HEAD movements always write that file, so the gate never misses one.

Merge the per-repo entries into one timestamp-ordered feed, newest first, with a 'since' cutoff — the cross-repo activity view. A repo with no reflog (a fresh 'git init', or 'core.logAllRefUpdates=false') contributes nothing and is not an error.
acceptance: In a tmp_path repo, a commit followed by a branch checkout produces two entries with verbs 'commit' and 'checkout', newest first, carrying unix timestamps. 'commit (initial)' normalises to verb 'commit'. A repo with '.git/logs' removed yields an empty list without raising. A second read with an unchanged '.git/logs/HEAD' mtime makes no git subprocess call (assert on a captured argv list).

title: Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
Derive last-edit recency from working-tree mtimes
description:
The reflog covers HEAD movements only. Editing a file in the working tree writes nothing under '.git', so a repo where someone has been editing for an hour without committing looks idle to the reflog. That repo is the most interesting row on the dashboard, so it cannot sort last.

Add to 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py' (or a small sibling module) a last-edit timestamp per repo: the newest mtime among the paths 'git status --porcelain=v2' already reported as modified, staged, unmerged or untracked. The paths come free with the status output the poller parses, so this costs one os.stat per dirty path and no extra git call.

Porcelain-v2 path fields: '1 ' and 'u ' lines end with a single path; '2 ' (rename/copy) lines end with two paths separated by a tab, and the first is the current one; '? ' lines are the path after the prefix. Paths are relative to the repo root and are quoted C-style when they contain unusual bytes — decode those rather than stat'ing the literal quoted string.

Cap the stat count per repo (a few hundred) so a repo with 50k untracked files does not stall the poll; when the cap is hit, use the newest mtime among the paths actually stat'ed and mark the value approximate.

The dashboard's recency ordering is then max(newest reflog timestamp, last-edit mtime), so a repo shows as recently active whether the work was committed or not.
acceptance: In a tmp_path repo with one committed file and one file modified just now, last_edit is within a second of now and later than the HEAD commit time. A clean repo yields last_edit=None. A rename staged with 'git mv' is stat'ed at its new path, not its old one. A path with a space and a path with a non-ASCII byte both stat successfully. Exceeding the stat cap returns a value flagged approximate instead of raising or hanging.

Textual dashboard over the live git poll
description:
The dashboard cboard2 exists for. Port the shape of '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/tui.py' (672 lines) onto the live poller instead of a SQLite reader.

New modules: 'src/cboard2/tui.py' (the Textual app) and 'src/cboard2/app.py' (the launcher that decides TUI versus CLI). Textual is imported from tui.py only, and 'pyproject.toml' gains 'textual' as a project dependency.

Main table columns: Repo, Branch, HEAD subject, Last commit, State (staged/unstaged/untracked counts), ahead/behind, Last active. Drop changeboard's Session column and its session filter — there is no session id without a hook.

Key bindings carried over: 'd' dirty only, 'u' unpushed only, 's' cycle sort (recent, name, dirty), 't' cycle time window, 'a' the cross-repo activity view, 'r' refresh now, 'enter' repo detail, 'q' quit.

Rows sort by recency = max(newest reflog timestamp, last-edit mtime), so uncommitted work ranks as activity.

The repo detail screen shows the changed files from the status output, the branch list from 'for-each-ref' with per-branch recency, and that repo's own reflog entries.

The activity view is the merged cross-repo reflog feed: timestamp, repo, verb, detail.

Poll on an interval (default 2s; measured 0.28s for 94 repos at 16 workers) in a worker so the UI never blocks on git. Two rules the port must keep: never run the poll on the UI thread, and never let one unreadable repo take down the refresh — show it flagged instead.
acceptance: Launching against a tmp roots tree lists every repo with live branch and dirty counts, no hook installed and no database file created anywhere. A commit made by an external 'git commit' appears in the activity view within one poll interval. 'd' hides clean repos and 'u' hides repos with nothing unpushed. A repo whose directory is deleted while the app runs is flagged rather than crashing the refresh. Tested with Textual's run_test() pilot, not by screenshot.

A repo whose directory is deleted while the app runs is flagged rather than crashing the refresh. Tested with Textual's run_test() pilot, not by screenshot.

Scripting subcommands: ls, json, busy
description:

'cboard2' with no subcommand launches the TUI. Otherwise:

title: Scripting subcommands: ls, json, busy
cboard2: hookless multi-repo git dashboard
description:
Rebuild changeboard (~/git/changeboard) so it needs no Claude Code hook. changeboard relies on a PostToolUse(Bash|Edit|Write) hook that snapshots git state into a shared SQLite store; only repos an agent touched ever appear. cboard2 derives everything from git and the filesystem instead, so every clone on disk shows up whether or not an agent has been near it.

Design decisions, measured on the author's machine (94 repos in ~/git, 109 under $HOME at depth 4):

- Current state comes from 'git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch' per repo. 0.28s for all 94 repos at 16 worker threads, so a 1-2s poll is affordable. --no-optional-locks matters: it stops the poller taking .git/index.lock and racing the user's own git commands.
- Recent activity comes from the reflog ('.git/logs/HEAD'), which records every HEAD movement with a unix timestamp and a verb: commit, checkout, merge, pull, rebase, reset, clone. This is the retroactive replacement for changeboard's 'events' table and its 'git_verb' column.
- Working-tree edits touch nothing under .git, so the reflog cannot see them. The newest mtime among the paths 'git status' reports as modified or untracked stands in for 'last edited'.

What carries over from changeboard: the Textual table (repo, branch, HEAD subject, dirty state, ahead/behind, recency), the dirty/unpushed filters, the sort cycle, the detail screen, and the scripting subcommands (ls, json, busy).

What is dropped: the hook, the collector, the SQLite store, the 'session' column and session filter (there is no session without a hook), 'prune', and 'add'/'forget' as store operations (discovery replaces them; ignore rules replace 'forget').

'ignore_repo' is what replaces changeboard's 'forget' command — a repo listed there is dropped during the discovery walk, so it costs no git subprocess call per poll. title: cboard2: hookless multi-repo git dashboard
Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
description:
cboard2 has no hook, so it cannot learn about repos from agent activity. It finds them by walking the filesystem.

New module: 'src/cboard2/discovery.py'.

Walk each configured root, prune at any directory containing a '.git' entry (do not descend into a repo looking for nested ones), and return the repo roots. Measured cost on the author's machine: 'find ~ -maxdepth 4 -name .git -type d -prune' returns 109 repos in 0.3s, so a plain os.scandir walk with a depth cap is fast enough to run at startup.

Config lives at '$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cboard2/config.toml' (falling back to '~/.config'), read with tomllib from the standard library:

  roots = ["~/git"]
  max_depth = 4
  ignore_repo = ["~/git/_old", "~/git/archived-thing"]

Defaults when the file is absent: roots = ['~'], max_depth = 4, ignore_repo = []. Expand '~' in every path.

An 'ignore_repo' entry matches a repo root exactly, or any repo beneath that path when the entry names a parent directory. An ignored repo is dropped during the walk, before it reaches the poller: it costs zero git subprocess calls per poll, not merely a hidden table row. This is the point of the option — a repo nobody touches any more should not cost a 'git status' every second.

Cache the discovered paths as JSON at '$XDG_CACHE_HOME/cboard2/repos.json' so a restart renders before the walk finishes. The cache is disposable: a missing or corrupt file means rescan, never an error. Prune paths that no longer exist on disk.

Env override 'CBOARD2_CONFIG' points at an alternate config file, for tests.
acceptance: discover() on a tmp_path tree containing two repos, a nested repo inside one of them, and a plain directory returns exactly the two outer repo roots. An 'ignore_repo' entry naming a repo root excludes that repo; an entry naming a parent directory excludes every repo under it. A test asserts an ignored repo produces no git subprocess call across a full poll cycle. A corrupt repos.json triggers a rescan rather than raising. A missing config file yields the documented defaults.

title: Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
description:
The dashboard's live columns (branch, dirty counts, ahead/behind, HEAD subject) come from polling git directly. There is no stored snapshot to read.

New module: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'.

Per repo, one call: 'git --no-optional-locks -C <root> status --porcelain=v2 --branch'. The '--no-optional-locks' flag is not optional here: without it the poller refreshes and rewrites '.git/index', taking 'index.lock' and racing whatever git command the user is running in that repo. git added the flag for exactly this class of status-bar tool.

The porcelain-v2 parser in '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/collector.py' (parse_porcelain_v2, _parse_ab) is correct and worth porting: it reads '# branch.head' (with the '(detached)' case), '# branch.oid' (with '(initial)'), '# branch.upstream', '# branch.ab', then counts staged/unstaged from the XY field of '1 '/'2 ' lines, unmerged from 'u ' lines, untracked from '? ' lines.

HEAD subject and commit time need a second call: 'git -C <root> log -1 --format=%s%x09%ct'. Return None for both when it fails, which is what an empty repo with no HEAD does.

Run the repos through a ThreadPoolExecutor. Measured: 94 repos in 0.28s at 16 workers, versus 1.4s serial. A repo whose git calls fail or time out (5s) is reported as unreadable rather than dropped, so a broken clone stays visible.

Expose a frozen dataclass RepoState carrying: path, name, branch, detached, head_sha, head_subject, head_time, staged, unstaged, untracked, ahead, behind, upstream. No last_touched or last_session fields — recency comes from the activity reader, and there are no sessions without a hook.
acceptance: poll() over a tmp_path tree with one dormant and one normal repo polls both on the first tick. On a second tick one second later, the normal repo is polled again and the dormant repo is not (assert on captured argv). Advancing the clock past dormant_interval polls the dormant repo again. poll(force=True) polls the dormant repo regardless of the window. Plus the original criteria: staged=1/unstaged=1/untracked=1 counts on a mixed working tree, detached HEAD sets detached=True and branch=None, a repo with no commits yields head_sha=None without raising, a non-repo path is reported unreadable rather than dropped, and every git invocation includes --no-optional-locks.
notes:
Per-repo poll scheduling, from the 'dormant' config key (see cboard2-1281):

A repo flagged dormant is polled at most once per 'dormant_interval' (default 4h) instead of once per poll tick. Track a last-polled timestamp per repo and skip a dormant repo whose last poll is inside the window, so it contributes no git subprocess call on the vast majority of ticks. That is the point of the key: 94 repos cost 0.28s per tick, and a user with several hundred mostly-archived clones should not pay for the archived ones every second.

A dormant repo still occupies a row. It shows its last known state and how old that reading is, so the dashboard never implies a stale row is current.

poll() takes a 'force' flag that ignores the dormant window and polls everything — this is what the TUI's shift+R binding calls (cboard2-2om0). Keep the decision in one predicate (something like 'due(repo, now)') rather than spread across the poll loop, so both the interval and the force path have one place to be tested.

title: Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
Textual dashboard over the live git poll
description:
The dashboard cboard2 exists for. Port the shape of '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/tui.py' (672 lines) onto the live poller instead of a SQLite reader.

New modules: 'src/cboard2/tui.py' (the Textual app) and 'src/cboard2/app.py' (the launcher that decides TUI versus CLI). Textual is imported from tui.py only, and 'pyproject.toml' gains 'textual' as a project dependency.

Main table columns: Repo, Branch, HEAD subject, Last commit, State (staged/unstaged/untracked counts), ahead/behind, Last active. Drop changeboard's Session column and its session filter — there is no session id without a hook.

Key bindings carried over: 'd' dirty only, 'u' unpushed only, 's' cycle sort (recent, name, dirty), 't' cycle time window, 'a' the cross-repo activity view, 'r' refresh now, 'enter' repo detail, 'q' quit.

Rows sort by recency = max(newest reflog timestamp, last-edit mtime), so uncommitted work ranks as activity.

The repo detail screen shows the changed files from the status output, the branch list from 'for-each-ref' with per-branch recency, and that repo's own reflog entries.

The activity view is the merged cross-repo reflog feed: timestamp, repo, verb, detail.

Poll on an interval (default 2s; measured 0.28s for 94 repos at 16 workers) in a worker so the UI never blocks on git. Two rules the port must keep: never run the poll on the UI thread, and never let one unreadable repo take down the refresh — show it flagged instead.
acceptance: Launching against a tmp roots tree lists every repo with live branch and dirty counts, no hook installed and no database file created anywhere. A commit made by an external 'git commit' appears in the activity view within one poll interval. 'd' hides clean repos and 'u' hides repos with nothing unpushed. A repo whose directory is deleted while the app runs is flagged rather than crashing the refresh. Tested with Textual's run_test() pilot, not by screenshot.
notes:
Two refresh bindings, not one:

- 'r' refreshes now, honoring the dormant window — dormant repos stay skipped.
- 'shift+R' forces a full refresh, polling every repo including dormant ones. It calls poll(force=True) from cboard2-on5y.

Textual spells the second binding 'R' in a Binding key string; keep both in the footer with distinct descriptions ('Refresh' and 'Refresh all') so the difference is visible without reading the source.

A dormant row shows the age of its reading in the Last active column, so a four-hour-old snapshot never reads as current. Dormant rows are listed like any other — the key changes poll frequency, not visibility.

title: Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
description:
cboard2 has no hook, so it cannot learn about repos from agent activity. It finds them by walking the filesystem.

New module: 'src/cboard2/discovery.py'.

Walk each configured root, prune at any directory containing a '.git' entry (do not descend into a repo looking for nested ones), and return the repo roots. Measured cost on the author's machine: 'find ~ -maxdepth 4 -name .git -type d -prune' returns 109 repos in 0.3s, so a plain os.scandir walk with a depth cap is fast enough to run at startup.

Config lives at '$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/cboard2/config.toml' (falling back to '~/.config'), read with tomllib from the standard library:

  max_depth = 4
  dormant = ["~/git/_old", "~/git/archived-thing"]
  dormant_interval = "4h"

title: Discover git repos by scanning configured roots
Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
description:
The dashboard's live columns (branch, dirty counts, ahead/behind, HEAD subject) come from polling git directly. There is no stored snapshot to read.

New module: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'.

Per repo, one call: 'git --no-optional-locks -C <root> status --porcelain=v2 --branch'. The '--no-optional-locks' flag is not optional here: without it the poller refreshes and rewrites '.git/index', taking 'index.lock' and racing whatever git command the user is running in that repo. git added the flag for exactly this class of status-bar tool.

The porcelain-v2 parser in '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/collector.py' (parse_porcelain_v2, _parse_ab) is correct and worth porting: it reads '# branch.head' (with the '(detached)' case), '# branch.oid' (with '(initial)'), '# branch.upstream', '# branch.ab', then counts staged/unstaged from the XY field of '1 '/'2 ' lines, unmerged from 'u ' lines, untracked from '? ' lines.

HEAD subject and commit time need a second call: 'git -C <root> log -1 --format=%s%x09%ct'. Return None for both when it fails, which is what an empty repo with no HEAD does.

Run the repos through a ThreadPoolExecutor. Measured: 94 repos in 0.28s at 16 workers, versus 1.4s serial. A repo whose git calls fail or time out (5s) is reported as unreadable rather than dropped, so a broken clone stays visible.

Expose a frozen dataclass RepoState carrying: path, name, branch, detached, head_sha, head_subject, head_time, staged, unstaged, untracked, ahead, behind, upstream. No last_touched or last_session fields — recency comes from the activity reader, and there are no sessions without a hook.
acceptance: poll() over a tmp_path tree with one dormant and one normal repo polls both on the first tick. On a second tick one second later, the normal repo is polled again and the dormant repo is not (assert on captured argv). Advancing the clock past dormant_interval polls the dormant repo again. poll(force=True) polls the dormant repo regardless of the window. Plus the original criteria: staged=1/unstaged=1/untracked=1 counts on a mixed working tree, detached HEAD sets detached=True and branch=None, a repo with no commits yields head_sha=None without raising, a non-repo path is reported unreadable rather than dropped, and every git invocation includes --no-optional-locks.
notes:
Per-repo poll scheduling, from the 'dormant' config key (see cboard2-1281):

A repo flagged dormant is polled at most once per 'dormant_interval' (default 4h) instead of once per poll tick. Track a last-polled timestamp per repo and skip a dormant repo whose last poll is inside the window, so it contributes no git subprocess call on the vast majority of ticks. That is the point of the key: 94 repos cost 0.28s per tick, and a user with several hundred mostly-archived clones should not pay for the archived ones every second.

A dormant repo still occupies a row. It shows its last known state and how old that reading is, so the dashboard never implies a stale row is current.

poll() takes a 'force' flag that ignores the dormant window and polls everything — this is what the TUI's shift+R binding calls (cboard2-2om0). Keep the decision in one predicate (something like 'due(repo, now)') rather than spread across the poll loop, so both the interval and the force path have one place to be tested.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

New file: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py' with 'RepoState', 'Snapshot', 'run_git', 'Poller' and 'parse_porcelain_v2'. Tests: 'tests/test_gitstate.py' (17 cases), plus 'git()', 'empty_git_repo' and 'git_repo' fixtures in 'tests/conftest.py' that run real git against a hermetic config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at /dev/null).

Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors, 0 warnings; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 52 passed in 0.61s.

End to end against the real repo set (load_config -> discover -> Poller.poll, no arguments anywhere):
  95 repos polled in 0.25s
  0 unreadable
  19 with uncommitted changes

That 0.25s matches the 0.28s the issue predicted from the shell measurement.

Design notes for whoever reads the module:

- 'due(repo, now)' is the single predicate the issue asked for. A non-dormant repo is always due; a dormant one is due when never polled or when its last reading is older than the interval. 'poll(force=True)' bypasses it.
- The Poller holds the last reading and last poll time per repo, so a skipped dormant repo still returns a row carrying its 'polled_at'. That is what lets the TUI show the age of a stale reading instead of implying it is current.
- Dropping a repo from the watch list forgets its cached reading, so a repo that goes dormant-then-deleted-then-back is polled fresh rather than showing a reading from before.
- Git failures are converted to 'readable=False' rather than exceptions, and '_snapshot' also catches OSError and ValueError, so one broken clone cannot take down a whole poll.
- 'run_git' is injectable ('runner=') so the scheduling tests assert on recorded argv without spawning git. A separate test monkeypatches subprocess.run to prove every real invocation starts with 'git --no-optional-locks'.

title: Read recent activity from each repo's reflog
description:
This replaces changeboard's whole hook-and-events mechanism. changeboard recorded a 'git_verb' per bash command into a SQLite 'events' table; git already keeps that log itself, in the reflog, with better coverage and full history.

New module: 'src/cboard2/activity.py'.

Read HEAD movements with 'git -C <root> reflog --date=unix --format=%gd%x09%ct%x09%gs%x09%h' (verified working). The '%gs' selector carries the verb and its detail, in forms like:

  commit: Add cboard add command
  commit (initial): Initial project setup
  checkout: moving from main to feature-x
  pull --rebase: Fast-forward
  reset: moving to HEAD~1

Parse the leading token up to ':' as the verb, keep the rest as detail, and normalise 'commit (initial)' and 'commit (amend)' to 'commit'. Timestamps are unix seconds from '%ct'.

Two more cheap sources belong here:

- Per-branch recency, one call: 'git -C <root> for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate refs/heads --format=%(refname:short)|%(committerdate:unix)|%(subject)'. Feeds the detail view.
- Last fetch: the mtime of '.git/FETCH_HEAD'. There is no reflog entry for a fetch that moved nothing.

Reading the reflog for 100 repos on every poll is wasteful. Gate it on the mtime of '.git/logs/HEAD': re-read a repo only when that mtime has moved since the last read. HEAD movements always write that file, so the gate never misses one.

Merge the per-repo entries into one timestamp-ordered feed, newest first, with a 'since' cutoff — the cross-repo activity view. A repo with no reflog (a fresh 'git init', or 'core.logAllRefUpdates=false') contributes nothing and is not an error.
acceptance: In a tmp_path repo, a commit followed by a branch checkout produces two entries with verbs 'commit' and 'checkout', newest first, carrying unix timestamps. 'commit (initial)' normalises to verb 'commit'. A repo with '.git/logs' removed yields an empty list without raising. A second read with an unchanged '.git/logs/HEAD' mtime makes no git subprocess call (assert on a captured argv list).

comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

New file: 'src/cboard2/activity.py' with 'Entry', 'Branch', 'ActivityReader', 'read_reflog', 'branches', 'last_fetch', 'log_mtime', 'git_dir' and 'split_message'. Tests: 'tests/test_activity.py' (14 cases). 'RecordingRunner' moved from 'tests/test_gitstate.py' into 'tests/conftest.py' so both modules share one fake git.

Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 66 passed in 0.64s.

Against the real repo set (95 repos, no arguments):
  cold read 1.45s, second read 0.001s
  verbs seen across every reflog: branch, checkout, cherry-pick, clone, commit, merge, pull, rebase, reset, revert

The 0.001s second read is the mtime gate working: 95 stat calls and no git process.

Three things worth knowing:

1. The reflog entry time comes from '%gd' under '--date=unix', which renders as 'HEAD@{1788524131}' and is parsed out of the braces. '%ct' looks equivalent and is not — it is the commit object's time, so a checkout of an old commit would be timestamped in the past. Verified the difference in a scratch repo before choosing.
2. Verbs are lowercased. git writes 'Branch: renamed refs/heads/a to refs/heads/b' with a capital and every other verb without one, which showed up as a stray 'Branch' verb in the first real run.
3. 'git_dir()' follows a '.git' file's 'gitdir:' pointer without spawning git, so a submodule's reflog is found and the mtime gate still works there. Reading the file is cheaper than 'git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir' on the poll path.

'Entry.repo_path' is in 'vulture_whitelist.py': the field is for the dashboard's activity view (cboard2-2om0) and nothing consumes it yet.

title: Derive last-edit recency from working-tree mtimes
description:
The reflog covers HEAD movements only. Editing a file in the working tree writes nothing under '.git', so a repo where someone has been editing for an hour without committing looks idle to the reflog. That repo is the most interesting row on the dashboard, so it cannot sort last.

Add to 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py' (or a small sibling module) a last-edit timestamp per repo: the newest mtime among the paths 'git status --porcelain=v2' already reported as modified, staged, unmerged or untracked. The paths come free with the status output the poller parses, so this costs one os.stat per dirty path and no extra git call.

  09-04 12:02 edit  keyforge                    d2
  09-04 11:56 head  analytics-charts                   d0

title: Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
description:
The dashboard's live columns (branch, dirty counts, ahead/behind, HEAD subject) come from polling git directly. There is no stored snapshot to read.

New module: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'.

Per repo, one call: 'git --no-optional-locks -C <root> status --porcelain=v2 --branch'. The '--no-optional-locks' flag is not optional here: without it the poller refreshes and rewrites '.git/index', taking 'index.lock' and racing whatever git command the user is running in that repo. git added the flag for exactly this class of status-bar tool.

The porcelain-v2 parser in '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/collector.py' (parse_porcelain_v2, _parse_ab) is correct and worth porting: it reads '# branch.head' (with the '(detached)' case), '# branch.oid' (with '(initial)'), '# branch.upstream', '# branch.ab', then counts staged/unstaged from the XY field of '1 '/'2 ' lines, unmerged from 'u ' lines, untracked from '? ' lines.

HEAD subject and commit time need a second call: 'git -C <root> log -1 --format=%s%x09%ct'. Return None for both when it fails, which is what an empty repo with no HEAD does.

Run the repos through a ThreadPoolExecutor. Measured: 94 repos in 0.28s at 16 workers, versus 1.4s serial. A repo whose git calls fail or time out (5s) is reported as unreadable rather than dropped, so a broken clone stays visible.

Expose a frozen dataclass RepoState carrying: path, name, branch, detached, head_sha, head_subject, head_time, staged, unstaged, untracked, ahead, behind, upstream. No last_touched or last_session fields — recency comes from the activity reader, and there are no sessions without a hook.
acceptance: poll() over a tmp_path tree with one dormant and one normal repo polls both on the first tick. On a second tick one second later, the normal repo is polled again and the dormant repo is not (assert on captured argv). Advancing the clock past dormant_interval polls the dormant repo again. poll(force=True) polls the dormant repo regardless of the window. Plus the original criteria: staged=1/unstaged=1/untracked=1 counts on a mixed working tree, detached HEAD sets detached=True and branch=None, a repo with no commits yields head_sha=None without raising, a non-repo path is reported unreadable rather than dropped, and every git invocation includes --no-optional-locks.
notes:
Per-repo poll scheduling, from the 'dormant' config key (see cboard2-1281):

A repo flagged dormant is polled at most once per 'dormant_interval' (default 4h) instead of once per poll tick. Track a last-polled timestamp per repo and skip a dormant repo whose last poll is inside the window, so it contributes no git subprocess call on the vast majority of ticks. That is the point of the key: 94 repos cost 0.28s per tick, and a user with several hundred mostly-archived clones should not pay for the archived ones every second.

A dormant repo still occupies a row. It shows its last known state and how old that reading is, so the dashboard never implies a stale row is current.

poll() takes a 'force' flag that ignores the dormant window and polls everything — this is what the TUI's shift+R binding calls (cboard2-2om0). Keep the decision in one predicate (something like 'due(repo, now)') rather than spread across the poll loop, so both the interval and the force path have one place to be tested.
closed_reason: Poller implemented with dormant scheduling, --no-optional-locks on every call, and a thread pool. 95 real repos in 0.24s.

comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

New file: 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py' with 'RepoState', 'Snapshot', 'run_git', 'Poller' and 'parse_porcelain_v2'. Tests: 'tests/test_gitstate.py' (17 cases), plus 'git()', 'empty_git_repo' and 'git_repo' fixtures in 'tests/conftest.py' that run real git against a hermetic config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM pointed at /dev/null).

Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors, 0 warnings; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 52 passed in 0.61s.

End to end against the real repo set (load_config -> discover -> Poller.poll, no arguments anywhere):
  95 repos polled in 0.25s
  0 unreadable
  19 with uncommitted changes

That 0.25s matches the 0.28s the issue predicted from the shell measurement.

Design notes for whoever reads the module:

- 'due(repo, now)' is the single predicate the issue asked for. A non-dormant repo is always due; a dormant one is due when never polled or when its last reading is older than the interval. 'poll(force=True)' bypasses it.
- The Poller holds the last reading and last poll time per repo, so a skipped dormant repo still returns a row carrying its 'polled_at'. That is what lets the TUI show the age of a stale reading instead of implying it is current.
- Dropping a repo from the watch list forgets its cached reading, so a repo that goes dormant-then-deleted-then-back is polled fresh rather than showing a reading from before.
- Git failures are converted to 'readable=False' rather than exceptions, and '_snapshot' also catches OSError and ValueError, so one broken clone cannot take down a whole poll.
- 'run_git' is injectable ('runner=') so the scheduling tests assert on recorded argv without spawning git. A separate test monkeypatches subprocess.run to prove every real invocation starts with 'git --no-optional-locks'.

title: Poll git state for every discovered repo in a thread pool
Read recent activity from each repo's reflog
description:
This replaces changeboard's whole hook-and-events mechanism. changeboard recorded a 'git_verb' per bash command into a SQLite 'events' table; git already keeps that log itself, in the reflog, with better coverage and full history.

New module: 'src/cboard2/activity.py'.

Read HEAD movements with 'git -C <root> reflog --date=unix --format=%gd%x09%ct%x09%gs%x09%h' (verified working). The '%gs' selector carries the verb and its detail, in forms like:

  commit: Add cboard add command
  commit (initial): Initial project setup
  checkout: moving from main to feature-x
  pull --rebase: Fast-forward
  reset: moving to HEAD~1

Parse the leading token up to ':' as the verb, keep the rest as detail, and normalise 'commit (initial)' and 'commit (amend)' to 'commit'. Timestamps are unix seconds from '%ct'.

Two more cheap sources belong here:

- Per-branch recency, one call: 'git -C <root> for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate refs/heads --format=%(refname:short)|%(committerdate:unix)|%(subject)'. Feeds the detail view.
- Last fetch: the mtime of '.git/FETCH_HEAD'. There is no reflog entry for a fetch that moved nothing.

Reading the reflog for 100 repos on every poll is wasteful. Gate it on the mtime of '.git/logs/HEAD': re-read a repo only when that mtime has moved since the last read. HEAD movements always write that file, so the gate never misses one.

Merge the per-repo entries into one timestamp-ordered feed, newest first, with a 'since' cutoff — the cross-repo activity view. A repo with no reflog (a fresh 'git init', or 'core.logAllRefUpdates=false') contributes nothing and is not an error.
acceptance: In a tmp_path repo, a commit followed by a branch checkout produces two entries with verbs 'commit' and 'checkout', newest first, carrying unix timestamps. 'commit (initial)' normalises to verb 'commit'. A repo with '.git/logs' removed yields an empty list without raising. A second read with an unchanged '.git/logs/HEAD' mtime makes no git subprocess call (assert on a captured argv list).
closed_reason: Reflog reader implemented with the logs/HEAD mtime gate. Cold read 1.45s over 95 repos, warm 0.001s.

1. The reflog entry time comes from '%gd' under '--date=unix', which renders as 'HEAD@{1788524131}' and is parsed out of the braces. 2. Verbs are lowercased. git writes 'Branch: renamed refs/heads/a to refs/heads/b' with a capital and every other verb without one, which showed up as a stray 'Branch' verb in the first real run.
3. 'git_dir()' follows a '.git' file's 'gitdir:' pointer without spawning git, so a submodule's reflog is found and the mtime gate still works there. Reading the file is cheaper than 'git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir' on the poll path.

'Entry.repo_path' is in 'vulture_whitelist.py': the field is for the dashboard's activity view (cboard2-2om0) and nothing consumes it yet.

Textual dashboard over the live git poll
description:
The dashboard cboard2 exists for. Port the shape of '~/git/changeboard/src/changeboard/tui.py' (672 lines) onto the live poller instead of a SQLite reader.

New modules: 'src/cboard2/tui.py' (the Textual app) and 'src/cboard2/app.py' (the launcher that decides TUI versus CLI). Textual is imported from tui.py only, and 'pyproject.toml' gains 'textual' as a project dependency.

Main table columns: Repo, Branch, HEAD subject, Last commit, State (staged/unstaged/untracked counts), ahead/behind, Last active. Drop changeboard's Session column and its session filter — there is no session id without a hook.

Key bindings carried over: 'd' dirty only, 'u' unpushed only, 's' cycle sort (recent, name, dirty), 't' cycle time window, 'a' the cross-repo activity view, 'r' refresh now, 'enter' repo detail, 'q' quit.

Rows sort by recency = max(newest reflog timestamp, last-edit mtime), so uncommitted work ranks as activity.

The repo detail screen shows the changed files from the status output, the branch list from 'for-each-ref' with per-branch recency, and that repo's own reflog entries.

The activity view is the merged cross-repo reflog feed: timestamp, repo, verb, detail.

Poll on an interval (default 2s; measured 0.28s for 94 repos at 16 workers) in a worker so the UI never blocks on git. Two rules the port must keep: never run the poll on the UI thread, and never let one unreadable repo take down the refresh — show it flagged instead.
acceptance: Launching against a tmp roots tree lists every repo with live branch and dirty counts, no hook installed and no database file created anywhere. A commit made by an external 'git commit' appears in the activity view within one poll interval. 'd' hides clean repos and 'u' hides repos with nothing unpushed. A repo whose directory is deleted while the app runs is flagged rather than crashing the refresh. Tested with Textual's run_test() pilot, not by screenshot.
notes:
Two refresh bindings, not one:

- 'r' refreshes now, honoring the dormant window — dormant repos stay skipped.
- 'shift+R' forces a full refresh, polling every repo including dormant ones. It calls poll(force=True) from cboard2-on5y.

Textual spells the second binding 'R' in a Binding key string; keep both in the footer with distinct descriptions ('Refresh' and 'Refresh all') so the difference is visible without reading the source.

A dormant row shows the age of its reading in the Last active column, so a four-hour-old snapshot never reads as current. Dormant rows are listed like any other — the key changes poll frequency, not visibility.

New files: 'src/cboard2/tui.py' (the Textual app, the detail modal and the activity modal) and 'src/cboard2/app.py' (the launcher). Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 114 passed in 1.59s.

    cboard2                       master   Initial project setup   48m ago   S24     -   22s ago

  after s: sort: name
  after t: 6 rows   (active <1h)
  activity: 200 rows, newest 'platform-gitops commit Name every object the keyforge-dev vault holds'

title: Textual dashboard over the live git poll
Write the README for cboard2
description:
'README.md' is still the python-bootstrap scaffold stub: a title and three lines about 'uv sync' and 'just'. Everything below is implemented and working but undocumented for anyone who is not the author.

Reference: '~/git/changeboard/README.md' covers the same ground for the hook-based predecessor and is the shape to follow — a one-paragraph summary, a 'How it works' diagram, then a section per surface.

What the README has to say, and where the facts live:

1. What cboard2 is: a live dashboard of every git repo on disk. The difference from changeboard is the headline — no Claude Code hook, no SQLite store, no registration step. State is read from git and the filesystem on an interval, so a clone appears because it is on disk, not because an agent touched it.
2. How it works, replacing changeboard's hook diagram: config roots -> 'discovery' walks for '.git' -> 'gitstate.Poller' runs one 'git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain=v2 --branch' per repo in a thread pool -> 'activity.ActivityReader' reads each reflog, gated on the mtime of 'logs/HEAD' -> 'board.Board' merges them into rows -> the CLI or the Textual app renders. Measured numbers worth quoting: 95 repos polled in 0.24s, cold reflog read 1.45s, a quiet tick 0.001s, dashboard first paint 1.15s.
3. Configuration: the 'config.toml' location and all four keys — 'roots' (default '~/git'), 'max_depth' (4), 'dormant', 'dormant_interval' ('4h'). Explain 'dormant' properly: a listed repo is still discovered and still shown, it is just polled every four hours instead of every tick, and 'shift+R' wakes it. Note that the walk skips dot-directories and symlinked directories, and that naming one as an explicit root includes it.
4. The dashboard: the key table (q, d, u, s, t, a, r, shift+R, enter) and what the columns mean, including that a dormant row shows the age of its reading and a vanished repo shows '✗'.
5. The CLI: 'ls', 'json' and 'busy', the 'DUR' syntax, and a tmux statusline one-liner using 'busy' as changeboard's README does.
6. A 'Development' section keeping the existing 'just' targets.

Prose follows the earn-the-line rules the repo writes docs under.
acceptance: A reader who has never seen the project can install it, write a config.toml with a dormant entry, launch the dashboard and use every key binding from the README alone. Every number quoted in it is one measured in this repo, not an estimate. No mention of a hook, a collector or a database as parts of cboard2 — only in the sentence contrasting it with changeboard.

title: Write the README for cboard2
Dashboard loses the selected row on every poll
description:
Reported from real use: with the dashboard open, a change in any repo makes the table repaint and the selected row is lost.

Cause: 'CboardApp.render_rows' in 'src/cboard2/tui.py' calls 'table.clear()' and then re-adds every row on every poll. DataTable resets its cursor to row 0 when it is cleared, so the cursor and the scroll position both jump. With a 2s interval and 95 repos this happens constantly, and it happens even on a tick where nothing changed at all.

Two parts, both needed:

1. Skip the repaint when the visible rows are unchanged. Compute a signature over the rows that are about to be drawn — the cell values, or per row the path, branch, dirty counts, ahead/behind, head_sha and active_at — and return early when it matches the signature of what is already painted. This removes the flicker on the common quiet tick, where nothing on screen would differ.
2. Preserve the cursor across a repaint that does happen. Read the current row key before clearing, via 'table.coordinate_to_cell_key(table.cursor_coordinate).row_key', then after re-adding the rows move the cursor back with 'table.move_cursor(row=table.get_row_index(key))'. The rows are already keyed by 'str(state.path)'. Guard both calls: the cursor may be on no row when the table is empty, and the repo may have been filtered out or deleted between the two paints, in which case leaving the cursor where it lands is correct.

Part 1 alone still loses the cursor whenever a real change arrives, which is the reported case. Part 2 alone still repaints needlessly twice a second. Neither is sufficient on its own.

Relevant API, all present in textual 8.2.8: 'coordinate_to_cell_key', 'cursor_coordinate', 'get_row_index', 'move_cursor', 'is_valid_row_index'.
acceptance: A test moves the cursor to the second row, makes a change in a different repo, polls, and asserts the cursor is still on the same repo path rather than back at row 0. A second test polls twice with nothing changed and asserts the table was not rebuilt — assert on the signature short-circuit, or on a spy over 'add_row'. A third asserts that when the selected repo drops out of the visible set, the repaint does not raise. Existing dashboard tests still pass.

acceptance: A test moves the cursor to the second row, makes a change in a different repo, polls, and asserts the cursor is still on the same repo path rather than back at row 0. comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Fixed and verified.

'src/cboard2/tui.py': 'render_rows' now builds the cells first, compares them against the last painted signature, and only clears and re-adds when they differ. The three tests:

1. Two repos, cursor moved to row 1, a change made in the other repo, then a poll. The cursor is still on the same repo path. This is the reported case.
2. A repaint with nothing changed leaves the existing RowKey objects in place. Worth knowing because the filters, the sort and the window all change the subtitle while possibly leaving every row's text identical.

title: Dashboard loses the selected row on every poll
Discover only the direct children of a root
description:
The dashboard should list the repos in '~/git' and nothing nested below them. Right now 'max_depth' defaults to 4, so '~/git/_old/network-routing-overview' gets a row alongside '~/git/keyforge'.

Measured on the author's machine, roots=('~/git',):
  max_depth=1 -> 89 repos, every one a direct child of ~/git
  max_depth=2 or more -> 95 repos, the extra 6 nested, three of them under ~/git/_old

Change: 'DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH' in 'src/cboard2/config.py' goes from 4 to 1. The walk in 'src/cboard2/discovery.py' already stops correctly at that depth — it pushes a root's children at depth 1 and refuses to descend once depth reaches 'max_depth' — so no change is needed there, only in the default and in the tests that assert it.

The key stays configurable. Anyone keeping clones as '~/git/<org>/<repo>' sets 'max_depth = 2' and gets the old behaviour.

One consequence worth recording: this empties the main use of the 'dormant' key. The three repos under '~/git/_old' were the motivating example for polling something every four hours, and they now do not appear at all. 'dormant' still earns its place for an archived repo sitting directly in '~/git', so keep it.

'src/cboard2/config.py' carries a docstring on 'DEFAULT_ROOTS' explaining why it is '~/git' rather than '~'. 'DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH' needs the same treatment: say that 1 means direct children only, and that a nested layout wants 2.
acceptance: 'discover()' over a tree holding '<root>/alpha' and '<root>/shelf/beta' returns only 'alpha' under the default config. The existing 'test_max_depth_stops_the_walk' still passes. 'tests/test_config.py::test_missing_file_yields_defaults' asserts max_depth == 1. A config setting 'max_depth = 2' finds 'shelf/beta' again, proving the key still works. Run against the real '~/git': 89 repos, none of them below a direct child.

Dashboard rows jump when a watched repo changes
description:
Reported from real use, and a follow-on from cboard2-4n40: with the dashboard open, something happening in a watched repo makes the UI jump around. The selection is now kept (that was 4n40) but the view still moves.

Two causes, both in 'CboardApp.render_rows' in 'src/cboard2/tui.py':

1. Rows are sorted by recency, so any repo becoming active moves to the top and every row below it shifts. 'render_rows' does a full 'table.clear()' plus re-add whenever any cell differs, which re-applies the sort on every value change. The selected repo keeps the cursor but lands somewhere else on screen.
2. 'restore_cursor' calls 'table.move_cursor(row=index)'. Its 'scroll' argument defaults to True, so the viewport is scrolled to the cursor even when the user had scrolled elsewhere.

Fix, in two parts:

1. Update cells in place when the visible key set is unchanged. 'DataTable.update_cell(row_key, column_key, value)' writes one cell without touching row order, so a commit in another repo changes that repo's cells where they already are. Column keys come from 'table.ordered_columns'; row keys are already 'str(state.path)'. Compare the new cells against the stored 'Painted' signature per row and write only the cells that differ — the signature is already there from 4n40.
2. Keep a full rebuild for the cases that genuinely need one: a repo added or removed from the visible set, or the user changing sort, filter or window. In that path capture 'table.scroll_offset' before clearing and restore it after, and pass 'scroll=False' to 'move_cursor' so the viewport is not yanked.

The consequence to accept and document: with the recency sort, row order refreshes on 'r', 'R', 's', 't', 'd', 'u' or a repo joining or leaving the visible set, not on every commit. That is the point — a list that reorders under the pointer twice a second cannot be read.

API confirmed present in textual 8.2.8: 'update_cell', 'update_cell_at', 'ordered_columns', 'scroll_offset', and 'move_cursor(scroll=False)'.
acceptance: A test paints two repos, records the row order, makes a commit in the one sorted last, polls, and asserts the row order is unchanged while that repo's HEAD cell now shows the new subject. A second test scrolls the table, polls with a changed repo, and asserts 'scroll_offset' is unchanged. A third asserts a repo appearing in the visible set does trigger a reorder. Pressing 's' still reorders. The three tests from cboard2-4n40 still pass, and so do the rest of tests/test_tui.py.

comments.text:
Fixed and verified.

'src/cboard2/tui.py': 'render_rows' now writes changed cells in place through 'DataTable.update_cell' and only rebuilds when the visible key set changes or an explicit key asked for a fresh order. New methods 'rebuild' and 'write_changed'; the 'Painted' alias is now a dict keyed by row path. 'restore_cursor' passes 'scroll=False', and 'rebuild' captures and restores 'table.scroll_offset'. The five reordering keys (d, u, s, t) and both refresh keys (r, R) set a '_reorder' flag that the next paint consumes.

Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 124 passed in 1.62s.

Driven against the real repo set:
  before:     82 rows, cursor on wiz-azure-connector, scroll y=6
  after tick: order same=True, cursor same=True, scroll y=6
  after 's':  order changed=True, subtitle '82/82 repos - sort: name'

Five tests added to 'tests/test_tui.py':

1. Two synthetic rows; the second becomes the most recent, which a rebuild would move to the top. Order is unchanged and its Active cell reads '1m ago', so the cell was written where it already sat.

Note on the earlier tests: 'test_an_unchanged_poll_does_not_repaint' from cboard2-4n40 still passes and now exercises the explicit-refresh path, because pressing 'r' sets the reorder flag and so does rebuild the table.

title: Dashboard rows jump when a watched repo changes
Dashboard never rescans, so repos never appear or disappear
description:
Reported from real use: a row for '~/git/scratch/vendor-vpn' stayed on the dashboard after that directory was deleted, still showing the branch, HEAD subject and dirty count read at launch.

Cause, in 'Board.refresh' in 'src/cboard2/board.py':

    if not self._repos:
        self.rescan()

The walk runs once, on the first refresh, and never again. Every later poll iterates the same list, so:

- a repo deleted after launch keeps its row for the whole session, showing whatever was last read from it
- a repo cloned after launch never appears, however long the dashboard stays open
- 'Poller._forget_absent' and 'ActivityReader.forget_absent' never fire in a long session, because the list they prune against never shrinks

A fresh 'cboard2 ls' is correct, since a new process scans on its first refresh. Only the long-running dashboard is affected. Restarting it is the current workaround.

Fix:

1. Rescan on an interval, not once. A walk of '~/git' at depth 1 costs about 0.3s and does not need to run every 2s tick — every 30s is ample, or every Nth poll. Keep it in the worker thread with the poll; it must not run on the UI thread.
2. Rescan on the explicit refresh keys 'r' and 'shift+R', so a user who has just cloned something does not wait for the interval.
3. Decide what a vanished repo does, and say so in the code: it should leave the table on the next rescan rather than linger. The '✗ name' strike-through rendering in 'render_rows' then covers only the window between a deletion and the next rescan, which is what it was written for.

Note the interaction with cboard2-3ney: a rescan that adds or removes a repo changes the visible key set, which already forces a rebuild and a re-sort. That is correct — a repo joining or leaving is exactly when the order should be recomputed. A rescan that finds nothing new must not set the reorder flag, or the jumping comes back.
acceptance: A test opens the board over a tree with one repo, creates a second repo, advances past the rescan interval, polls, and asserts the new repo has a row. A second test deletes a repo the same way and asserts its row is gone rather than struck through forever. A third asserts a rescan that finds no change does not reorder the rows, so the cboard2-3ney tests still hold. A fourth asserts pressing 'r' rescans without waiting for the interval. Verified by hand against ~/git: clone something into it with the dashboard open and watch the row arrive.

title: Dashboard never rescans, so repos never appear or disappear
description:
Reported from real use: a row for '~/git/scratch/vendor-vpn' stayed on the dashboard after that directory was deleted, still showing the branch, HEAD subject and dirty count read at launch.

Cause, in 'Board.refresh' in 'src/cboard2/board.py':

    if not self._repos:
        self.rescan()

The walk runs once, on the first refresh, and never again. Every later poll iterates the same list, so:

- a repo deleted after launch keeps its row for the whole session, showing whatever was last read from it
- a repo cloned after launch never appears, however long the dashboard stays open
- 'Poller._forget_absent' and 'ActivityReader.forget_absent' never fire in a long session, because the list they prune against never shrinks

A fresh 'cboard2 ls' is correct, since a new process scans on its first refresh. Only the long-running dashboard is affected. Restarting it is the current workaround.

Fix:

1. Rescan on an interval, not once. A walk of '~/git' at depth 1 costs about 0.3s and does not need to run every 2s tick — every 30s is ample, or every Nth poll. Keep it in the worker thread with the poll; it must not run on the UI thread.
2. Rescan on the explicit refresh keys 'r' and 'shift+R', so a user who has just cloned something does not wait for the interval.
3. Decide what a vanished repo does, and say so in the code: it should leave the table on the next rescan rather than linger. The '✗ name' strike-through rendering in 'render_rows' then covers only the window between a deletion and the next rescan, which is what it was written for.

Note the interaction with cboard2-3ney: a rescan that adds or removes a repo changes the visible key set, which already forces a rebuild and a re-sort. That is correct — a repo joining or leaving is exactly when the order should be recomputed. A rescan that finds nothing new must not set the reorder flag, or the jumping comes back.
acceptance: A test opens the board over a tree with one repo, creates a second repo, advances past the rescan interval, polls, and asserts the new repo has a row. A second test deletes a repo the same way and asserts its row is gone rather than struck through forever. A third asserts a rescan that finds no change does not reorder the rows, so the cboard2-3ney tests still hold. A fourth asserts pressing 'r' rescans without waiting for the interval. Verified by hand against ~/git: clone something into it with the dashboard open and watch the row arrive.

title: Dashboard never rescans, so repos never appear or disappear
Toggle a repo dormant from the dashboard with shift+D
description:
Marking a repo dormant means hand-editing 'config.toml' today. The dashboard already knows which repo is selected, so it should be able to write the entry itself.

Binding: 'D' (shift+D), toggling the selected repo. Lowercase 'd' is the dirty filter and 'shift+R' is already the shifted sibling of 'r', so the scheme holds. 'ctrl+shift+d' was the original request and was dropped on purpose: it only reaches the app through the Kitty keyboard protocol, so it works in Ghostty and kitty and silently does nothing in Terminal.app, and some emulators bind it themselves for split-pane. Footer label: 'Dormant'.

Three parts:

1. A config writer, in 'src/cboard2/config.py' or a sibling. The stdlib has 'tomllib' for reading and no writer at all, and the user's live config carries comments explaining each key. So rewrite only the value of 'dormant' and leave every other byte of the file alone — do not regenerate the file from the parsed Config, which would delete the comments. Handle all three shapes the key can be in: absent entirely, a single-line array, and a multi-line array. When the key is absent, append it with a short comment. Write through a temp file in the same directory and 'replace()' it, the way 'discovery.write_cache' does, so an interrupted write cannot truncate the config.

2. The toggle action in 'src/cboard2/tui.py'. Read the selected row's path from the cursor — 'cursor_key' already returns it — add or remove it from 'config.dormant', write the file, and update the in-memory Config so the change applies without a restart. 'Config' is a frozen dataclass, so this is 'dataclasses.replace' plus handing the new Config to the Board. 'Board.config' is a plain attribute; 'Board._poller' holds 'dormant_interval' but not the dormant set, and 'Repo.dormant' is set during discovery, so the toggle has to force a rescan for the flag to reach the rows.

3. Feedback. The row's Active cell starts reading '(read …)' once the repo is skipped, which is only visible after the interval passes. Notify on the toggle so the user knows it landed: 'self.notify(f"{name} is now dormant")' or the reverse.

Interaction to respect: a dormant repo is still discovered and still gets a row (cboard2-1281 and cboard2-on5y). Toggling must not make it disappear. The rescan changes 'Repo.dormant' but not the visible key set, so cboard2-3ney's in-place path still applies and rows must not reorder.
acceptance: Pressing D on a selected repo writes its path into the dormant array in config.toml and notifies. Pressing D again removes it. A config file with comments above and below the dormant key keeps every comment byte-for-byte after both writes; assert on the full file text, not on the parsed value. A config with no dormant key at all gains one. A single-line 'dormant = []' and a multi-line array are both handled. After the toggle the repo's row is still present and the poller skips it on the next tick inside the interval. Rows do not reorder on the toggle. An unwritable config directory surfaces an error notification instead of raising.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Implemented and verified.

New file 'src/cboard2/configwrite.py': 'toggled', 'write_dormant', 'render', 'display', 'quote' and the span-finding helpers. 'src/cboard2/tui.py': 'Binding("D", "toggle_dormant", "Dormant")', 'action_toggle_dormant', and a 'config_file' constructor argument so tests can point at a temp file. Tests: new 'tests/test_configwrite.py' (11 cases) and 5 added to 'tests/test_tui.py'.

Checks, all clean: 'just lint' -> All checks passed; 'just lint-pyright' -> 0 errors; 'just vulture' -> no output; 'just test' -> 147 passed in 2.11s.

Verified on a synthetic three-repo tree with a counting subclass: one press of D fires the action exactly once, on the row under the cursor, and writes

  dormant = [
      "/tmp/toggle-tree/beta",
  ]

Verified again on a copy of the author's real config: D added the selected repo, every comment survived, the file parsed back, and a second D restored the file byte for byte.

Implementation notes:

1. Only the bytes of the 'dormant' value are replaced. '_key_span' locates the assignment and '_array_end' scans to the matching bracket, skipping quoted strings and comments so a ']' inside either does not end the scan early. Nothing else in the file is touched, which is why the comments survive — regenerating from the parsed Config would have deleted them.
2. 'dormant_interval' shares the first seven characters, so '_find_key' checks the character after the key before accepting a match. There is a test for it.
3. A missing key is inserted at the end of the top-level region, not appended to the file. Appending would land it inside the last '[table]', which is a different key that happens to share the name — the first version did exactly that and a test caught it.
4. Paths are written relative to home when they sit under it, so the file keeps reading like the hand-written '~/git' entries instead of expanding to absolute paths.
5. The toggle replaces 'Board.config' via 'dataclasses.replace' and calls 'poll(rescan=True)', because 'Repo.dormant' is set during discovery and only a rescan carries the new flag to the rows. It does not set the reorder flag, so rows stay put — there is a test for that.
6. 'ctrl+shift+d' was the original request and 'D' was chosen instead: 'ctrl+shift' only reaches an app through the Kitty keyboard protocol, so it works in Ghostty and kitty and silently does nothing in Terminal.app.

Note on testing notifications: toasts do not mount under 'run_test()', so 'tests/test_tui.py' has a 'RecordingApp' subclass that overrides 'notify' to record the message. That is the only public way to assert on what the app told the user.

The first populated frame of the dashboard takes about 1.0s on a 75-repo tree. Marking repos dormant does not help this: dormancy only affects repeat ticks, and it saves 0.071s there.

Measured on the author's machine (75 repos under ~/git and ~/git/personal, 12 dormant, max_depth 1):

  discover walk           0.005s
  git poll, 16 workers    0.239s
  reflog read, serial     0.605s
  boot + textual import   ~0.10s
  first populated frame   ~1.0s

  warm tick               0.167s
  warm tick, force=True   0.238s   (all repos, dormancy bypassed)

Cause: Board.refresh builds its rows in a list comprehension (src/cboard2/board.py:97) that calls ActivityReader.latest per repo. Each uncached call spawns one 'git reflog' subprocess, so 75 of them run one after another. Poller._snapshot_all already fans its two git calls out over a ThreadPoolExecutor at 16 workers (src/cboard2/gitstate.py:170); the reflog reads do not. Running the same 75 reads at 16 threads took 0.116s, which is 0.49s off cold start.

Dormancy cannot cover the cold path by design: Poller.due returns True when a repo has never been polled (src/cboard2/gitstate.py:139), and ActivityReader has no persisted cache at all, so every repo pays a reflog read on the first tick.

Second finding, same area: discovery.read_cache (src/cboard2/discovery.py:71) is called only from tests. Its docstring says 'so the first frame has rows', but no production code reads the cache — write_cache is called from Board.rescan and nothing consumes the file. Either wire it into the startup path or delete it with its docstring claim.
acceptance:
1. ActivityReader reads reflogs concurrently, matching Poller's worker pool, and Board.refresh no longer serializes them.
2. Cold first-frame time on a 75-repo tree drops below 0.5s, measured and cited in the review comment.
3. Warm tick time does not regress past 0.20s.
4. discovery.read_cache is either wired into the startup path or removed along with its tests and its 'first frame has rows' docstring claim; whichever is chosen is stated in the review comment.
5. Existing tests pass; ActivityReader's mtime gate and forget_absent still hold under concurrent reads.
notes: Reproduce with: uv run python -c on a script that times load_config, discover, Poller.poll and a loop of ActivityReader.latest over the discovered repos. The reflog stage is the one to watch.

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Done, measured on the same 75-repo tree.

  stage                    before    after
  first populated frame    0.903s    0.349-0.448s (median 0.37s)
  warm tick                0.164s    0.158-0.188s
  warm tick, force=True    0.238s    0.234-0.238s

Change 1 - ActivityReader.prime(repos) (src/cboard2/activity.py:93) collects the repos whose logs/HEAD moved since the last read and runs those reads over a ThreadPoolExecutor at 16 workers, matching Poller's pool. Board.refresh calls it before the row comprehension (src/cboard2/board.py:101), and feed calls it before merging, so the activity screen's first open is covered too. entries() is unchanged: after prime it finds every answer cached. The mtime gate still holds - a second prime with nothing moved spawns no git call.

Change 2 - deleted discovery.cache_path, read_cache and write_cache along with the CBOARD2_CACHE env var, the Board.rescan write call and the five cache tests. Chose deletion over wiring: the walk it would have skipped measures 0.005s on this tree, against the 0.605s the reflog reads cost, so the cache could not have paid for its own complexity. The TUI test that asserted one repos.json under XDG_CACHE_HOME now asserts the app writes nothing there at all, which is the stronger form of the same claim.

Tests: 145 passed. ruff format, ruff check, pyright and vulture all clean.

Acceptance: (1) done. (2) 0.37s median, below 0.5s. (3) 0.188s worst warm tick, below 0.20s. (4) removed, stated above. (5) 145 pass, prime's mtime gate and forget_absent covered by three new tests in tests/test_activity.py.

title: Cold start blocks the first frame for ~1s: reflog reads run serially
Flag repos whose local default branch is behind the remote
description:
cboard2 reports `behind` from `git status --porcelain=v2 --branch` (src/cboard2/gitstate.py, `_parse_ab`). That field compares HEAD against the LOCAL remote-tracking ref, so it stays wrong until something fetches. A user who has not fetched in a week sees `-0` and believes local main is current.

Add a read-only remote check that answers: has the newest main/master been pulled into this clone?

Transport, decided with the user: batched `gh api graphql` over every repo's origin, NOT `git fetch`. Measured on the author's machine: `git ls-remote` costs 1.7s per repo (66 repos would be ~8s of network and does not fit the 2s poll tick), while one aliased GraphQL query did 3 repos in 0.6s. `git fetch` is also rejected because it rewrites remote-tracking refs under the user.

All 66 repos with an origin under the author's ~/git point at github.com, so gh is the only backend needed. Degrade to 'unknown' when gh is missing, unauthed, or the origin is not GitHub — never error out of a poll.

Design:
- New module `src/cboard2/remote.py`, holding a reader with the same injected-runner shape as `gitstate.Poller` (a `runner` for git, a separate callable for gh) so tests need no network.
- Per repo, locally and in a thread pool: `git remote get-url origin` for owner/name, and `git for-each-ref refs/heads` for local branch tips.
- One batched GraphQL query, chunked, for each repo's `defaultBranchRef { name target { oid } }`.
- Stale means: the local ref named by the remote default branch exists, its sha differs from the remote sha, AND the remote sha is absent from the local object store (`git cat-file -e <sha>^{commit}`). That last test is what separates 'not pulled' from 'local main is ahead' without fetching.
- Runs on its own slow interval (config key `remote_interval`, default 5m) plus the existing refresh-all key, never on the 2s tick.

Surface, decided with the user: a new `Remote` column in the TUI table marking a stale default branch, a filter key limiting the table to those repos, the same signal in the per-repo detail panel, and matching fields in `cboard2 ls`/`json` behind an explicit `--remote` flag (a bare `ls` must stay network-free for tmux statuslines).

Acceptance criteria:
- A clone whose local main lacks the remote's newest main commit is marked stale.
- A clone that is level, or whose local main is ahead, is not marked stale.
- A repo with no origin, a non-GitHub origin, or no local default branch reads as unknown, not stale.
- `gh` absent or unauthed leaves every repo unknown and logs nothing to the table.
- A bare `cboard2 ls` makes no network call.
- `just lint-all`, `just vulture` and `just test` pass.

title: Flag repos whose local default branch is behind the remote
Show the user's own open and draft PRs per repo
description:
cboard2 shows local git state only, so a PR left open or a draft left parked is invisible until the user opens GitHub. Surface both per repo.

Transport, decided with the user: ONE `gh search prs --author=@me --state=open --json number,title,isDraft,repository,url,updatedAt --limit 100` call for every repo at once, NOT `gh pr list` per repo. Measured on the author's machine: the single search returned 23 open PRs (5 of them drafts) across all repos in 1.5s; 66 per-repo calls would be far slower and burn rate limit.

All 66 repos with an origin under the author's ~/git point at github.com, so gh is the only backend needed.

Design:
- Lives in the same new `src/cboard2/remote.py` as issue cboard2-55f0, sharing its reader, its injected gh callable and its slow refresh interval (config key `remote_interval`, default 5m). Do cboard2-55f0 first or alongside; the module skeleton comes from it.
- Match a search result to a repo by `repository.nameWithOwner` against the owner/name parsed from that repo's `git remote get-url origin`. The directory name is not the repo name — `~/git/certbot` has origin `example-org/acmebot` — so never match on directory name.
- Two clones of the same repo both match the same PRs. That is correct, not a bug to guard.
- Keep number, title, url, draft flag and updated time per PR.
- Degrade to 'unknown' when gh is missing, unauthed, or the search fails. Never error out of a poll.

Surface, decided with the user: a new `PR` column in the TUI table showing the open count with the draft count beside it, a filter key limiting the table to repos with open PRs, the full list (number, title, draft marker, url) in the per-repo detail panel, and matching fields in `cboard2 ls`/`json` behind the same explicit `--remote` flag, so a bare `ls` stays network-free.

Acceptance criteria:
- A repo with two open PRs, one of them a draft, shows both counts.
- A repo with no open PRs of the user's shows nothing, not a zero that reads as an error.
- PRs authored by someone else in the same repo are not counted.
- The detail panel lists each PR with its number, title, draft marker and url.
- `gh` absent or unauthed leaves the column unknown.
- A bare `cboard2 ls` makes no network call.
- `just lint-all`, `just vulture` and `just test` pass.

Cold start blocks the first frame for ~1s: reflog reads run serially
description:
The first populated frame of the dashboard takes about 1.0s on a 75-repo tree. Marking repos dormant does not help this: dormancy only affects repeat ticks, and it saves 0.071s there.

Measured on the author's machine (75 repos under ~/git and ~/git/personal, 12 dormant, max_depth 1):

  discover walk           0.005s
  git poll, 16 workers    0.239s
  reflog read, serial     0.605s
  boot + textual import   ~0.10s
  first populated frame   ~1.0s

  warm tick               0.167s
  warm tick, force=True   0.238s   (all repos, dormancy bypassed)

Cause: Board.refresh builds its rows in a list comprehension (src/cboard2/board.py:97) that calls ActivityReader.latest per repo. Each uncached call spawns one 'git reflog' subprocess, so 75 of them run one after another. Poller._snapshot_all already fans its two git calls out over a ThreadPoolExecutor at 16 workers (src/cboard2/gitstate.py:170); the reflog reads do not. Running the same 75 reads at 16 threads took 0.116s, which is 0.49s off cold start.

Dormancy cannot cover the cold path by design: Poller.due returns True when a repo has never been polled (src/cboard2/gitstate.py:139), and ActivityReader has no persisted cache at all, so every repo pays a reflog read on the first tick.

Second finding, same area: discovery.read_cache (src/cboard2/discovery.py:71) is called only from tests. Its docstring says 'so the first frame has rows', but no production code reads the cache — write_cache is called from Board.rescan and nothing consumes the file. Either wire it into the startup path or delete it with its docstring claim.
acceptance:
1. ActivityReader reads reflogs concurrently, matching Poller's worker pool, and Board.refresh no longer serializes them.
2. Cold first-frame time on a 75-repo tree drops below 0.5s, measured and cited in the review comment.
3. Warm tick time does not regress past 0.20s.
4. discovery.read_cache is either wired into the startup path or removed along with its tests and its 'first frame has rows' docstring claim; whichever is chosen is stated in the review comment.
5. Existing tests pass; ActivityReader's mtime gate and forget_absent still hold under concurrent reads.
notes: Reproduce with: uv run python -c on a script that times load_config, discover, Poller.poll and a loop of ActivityReader.latest over the discovered repos. The reflog stage is the one to watch.
closed_reason: Reflog reads now fan out over a 16-worker pool; first populated frame dropped from 0.903s to 0.37s median on a 75-repo tree. Unused discovery cache removed.
