comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
No-flash follow-up: origins are now read on the fast local clock, not the network one. RemoteReader._adopt_origins (src/cboard2/remote.py) runs from refresh_local, asks git remote get-url once per repo and memoizes the answer in _origin_urls, so the first painted table already carries colors and the steady poll runs nothing extra. No cache entry was added: the origin is local git config, and a cache would still flash on a cold start. Measured over ~/git with remote = false: first refresh 0.43s for 40 rows, 38 with an origin, second refresh 0.16s.

Also added the config key origin_colors (default true) in src/cboard2/config.py, threaded through row_cells and painted_row and the detail panel, documented in README's key table. 366 tests pass; ruff, pyright and vulture clean.

Show conflicted, mid-merge and stashed state instead of folding it into dirty
description:
A repo with merge conflicts renders as ordinary dirty work. 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py:279' counts each 'u ' line from 'git status --porcelain=v2' into 'unstaged', so the conflict marker is lost before it reaches a row. Nothing reads '.git/MERGE_HEAD', '.git/rebase-merge' or '.git/rebase-apply' either, so a repo halted mid-rebase looks the same as one with edits in progress. Stashes are not counted at all.

The user opens the dashboard to decide which repo to return to. A conflicted or half-rebased repo needs attention before any other dirty repo, and right now the table cannot say so.

Work: add 'unmerged', 'operation' (none/merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect) and 'stashed' to RepoState in 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'; parse 'u ' lines separately in the porcelain reader around line 279; read the in-progress markers from the git dir; count stash entries from 'git stash list' or 'refs/stash'. Render the state in 'src/cboard2/cli.py' state_text and in the TUI table and detail screen in 'src/cboard2/tui.py'. Keep the per-repo cost inside the current poll budget (0.28s for 94 repos at 16 threads) -- prefer a filesystem check over an extra git call.
acceptance: A repo with a conflicted file shows a distinct marker in 'cboard2 ls' and in the dashboard row, not just a raised dirty count. A repo stopped mid-rebase says so. A repo with stashes shows the count. Tests in 'tests/test_gitstate.py' cover a 'u ' status line, each in-progress marker and a non-empty stash.

title: Show conflicted, mid-merge and stashed state instead of folding it into dirty
Filter the dashboard by repo name from the keyboard
description:
The dashboard has five boolean filters -- dirty, unpushed, behind, open PRs, dormant -- bound in 'src/cboard2/tui.py:509'. None of them narrows by name, so reaching one known repo among the ~94 under '~/git' means scrolling or cycling the sort.

Work: bind a key (suggest '/') to a single-line input over the table in 'src/cboard2/tui.py'. Match case-insensitively against the repo name, and clear on escape. The filter composes with the existing toggles rather than replacing them. Row identity already survives a poll (see cboard2-4n40 and cboard2-3ney) -- keep the selected row selected while the filter text changes.
acceptance: Pressing '/' in the dashboard opens an input; typing narrows the table to repos whose name contains the text, case-insensitively; escape clears it and restores the full list. The dirty/unpushed/behind/PR toggles still apply on top of the name filter. Tests in 'tests/test_tui.py' cover a match, a no-match empty table, composition with one toggle, and escape restoring the rows.

title: Filter the dashboard by repo name from the keyboard
Show PRs awaiting your review and each PR's checks status
description:
The remote read covers pull requests the user authored and nothing else -- 'src/cboard2/remote.py:102' documents PullRequest as 'One open pull request the user authored', and the search in 'parse_prs' ('remote.py:247') is built from that. Two things the user acts on are absent: a PR where someone requested their review, and whether a PR of theirs is red.

Work: add a second 'gh search prs' call for review-requested PRs, keyed by the same slug map, and ask for the rollup checks state on each PR in the GraphQL query ('build_query', 'remote.py:211'). Extend RemoteState ('remote.py:113') and Cached ('remote.py:150') with the new fields, and bump the cache shape so an old cache file on disk is discarded rather than misread. Render in 'src/cboard2/cli.py' pr_text and in the detail panel in 'src/cboard2/tui.py', keeping the OSC 8 links added by cboard2-5ytf. Respect PR_LIMIT and the gh timeout already in 'remote.py'.
acceptance: 'cboard2 ls --remote' and the detail panel show, per repo, the user's own open PRs and the PRs awaiting their review, distinguishable from each other. Each PR carries a passing/failing/pending checks marker. An old cache file from before this change does not crash a run. Tests in 'tests/test_remote.py' cover a review-requested PR, a failing checks rollup, a repo with both kinds, and a stale cache shape.

title: Show PRs awaiting your review and each PR's checks status
busy takes no --remote, so a script cannot ask whether anything needs attention remotely
description:
'cboard2 busy' exits 0 when any repo was active inside the window, and its parser is given 'remote=False, refresh=False' unconditionally at 'src/cboard2/cli.py:93'. 'ls' and 'json' both take '--remote' and '--refresh'. A prompt or status line that wants 'is anything behind the remote or waiting on an open PR' has to run 'cboard2 json --remote' and parse it.

Work: accept '--remote' and '--refresh' on the busy subparser in 'build_parser' ('src/cboard2/cli.py:72') and decide in 'cmd_busy' ('cli.py:139') what counts as busy when they are given -- a repo behind the remote or holding an open PR counts alongside recent local activity. Serve from the cache in 'src/cboard2/remotecache.py' unless '--refresh' is passed, so a per-prompt call costs no network.
acceptance: 'cboard2 busy --remote' exits 0 when a repo is behind its remote or has an open PR, even with no local activity in the window, and exits 1 when neither holds. Without '--remote' the exit code matches today's behaviour. Tests in 'tests/test_cli.py' cover each of those three cases and confirm '--remote' alone reads the cache without invoking gh.

title: busy takes no --remote, so a script cannot ask whether anything needs attention remotely
Behind count never updates for a branch that is not the default
description:
The ahead/behind pair comes from the remote-tracking ref that 'git status --branch' reports, and nothing in a poll fetches -- 'src/cboard2/remote.py:4' states this. The GitHub read in 'remote.py' covers the default branch only: it compares each repo's default-branch tip on GitHub against the local ref. The single fetch in the codebase is 'src/cboard2/pull.py:100', run from shift+P, which targets the default branch.

So a feature branch that gained commits on the remote reports behind=0 forever, and the 'u' (unpushed) filter is the only remote-aware signal a working branch has.

Work: extend the GraphQL query in 'build_query' ('src/cboard2/remote.py:211') to ask for the tip of the checked-out branch per repo alongside the default branch, or add a periodic 'git fetch --prune' on the remote_interval clock for non-dormant repos. Prefer the GraphQL route: it stays hookless and does not write to the repo. Reuse the disk cache in 'src/cboard2/remotecache.py' and the existing 'refresh_local' path so a pull clears the marker on the next poll rather than at the end of the network interval.
acceptance: A repo on a feature branch whose remote gained a commit shows a behind count in 'cboard2 ls --remote' and in the dashboard within one remote interval. A repo on its default branch keeps the behaviour it has today. Tests in 'tests/test_remote.py' cover a non-default branch that is behind, one that is level, and a branch with no remote counterpart.
notes: Delivered by af08e7b: RemoteState.branch_remote/branch_sha/branch_known/behind_branch, rendered by cli.remote_text and tui.remote_text, covered by tests/test_remote.py:1120-1200 (behind, level, no remote counterpart). The behind marker stays a boolean: remote.py never fetches, so the commits are not in the local object database to count. User chose the boolean over a GraphQL compare count on 2026-09-05.

Publish cboard2 to Homebrew
description:
Install today is `uv tool install .` from a clone (README.md:19). The goal is `brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2`, matching how dogcat ships.

dogcat already runs this pipeline end to end, so the work is porting it, not designing it. Read /Users/ove/git/dogcat/docs/releasing.md first, then .github/workflows/publish.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml in that repo.

How dogcat's chain works:
1. A merged PR from a `release/vX.Y.Z` branch fires publish.yml.
2. publish.yml tags vX.Y.Z, runs `uv build`, and creates a GitHub release carrying the wheel and sdist.
3. Its `update-homebrew` job downloads that wheel, computes its sha256, and sed-rewrites `url` and `sha256` in Formula/dogcat.rb in the oroddlokken/homebrew-tap repo, using secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN.
4. The formula (Language::Python::Virtualenv) builds a venv under libexec and pip-installs the pinned wheel.

The formula pins a GitHub release asset, not a PyPI URL, so Homebrew needs no PyPI account.

What cboard2 lacks: LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md, a release workflow, a version derived from git tags (pyproject.toml pins 0.1.0 by hand), a release-prep script, and a Formula/cboard2.rb in the tap. .github/workflows/ holds ci.yml only.
acceptance:
brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2 installs a working cboard2 on a clean machine
A tagged release updates the tap formula with no hand edit
README.md documents the brew install line

Derive the version from git tags with hatch-vcs
description:
pyproject.toml:3 pins `version = "0.1.0"` by hand. The release chain reads the version out of the tag and the branch name, so a hand-edited number drifts from the tag and the formula pins a wheel whose filename no longer matches.

Port the setup from /Users/ove/git/dogcat/pyproject.toml:

    [project]
    dynamic = ["version"]

    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs"]

    [tool.hatch.version]
    source = "vcs"
    raw-options = { version_scheme = "no-guess-dev" }

    [tool.hatch.build.hooks.vcs]
    version-file = "src/cboard2/_version.py"

Add the generated `_version.py` to .gitignore. Check whether any code reads a version string today (`grep -rn version src/cboard2`) and point it at the new module or at importlib.metadata.
acceptance:
uv build in a clone with tag v0.2.0 produces cboard2-0.2.0-py3-none-any.whl
src/cboard2/_version.py is gitignored and not committed
just lint-all and just test-all pass

Add CHANGELOG.md the release workflow can parse
description:
publish.yml builds the GitHub release body by awk-ing the section for the released version out of CHANGELOG.md (see /Users/ove/git/dogcat/.github/workflows/publish.yml, step "Extract changelog entry"). Without the file the release body is empty and the awk step still exits 0, so the gap shows only after publishing.

The awk matches lines starting with `## ` that contain the version string, and prints until the next `## `. Follow /Users/ove/git/dogcat/CHANGELOG.md exactly for the heading format.

Seed it with the entries covering the work already on main: worktrees as repo members, per-origin repo colors, the behind-its-own-remote column, ls-remote default branches.

description:
This is the workflow the whole epic hangs on. Port /Users/ove/git/dogcat/.github/workflows/publish.yml, dropping the parts cboard2 has no use for: the pnpm and node steps (cboard2 lints no JS), the publish-pypi job, and the sdist check that only guards PyPI.

Trigger: pull_request closed on main, `if: merged == true && startsWith(github.head_ref, 'release/v')`. The branch name is the version source — landing the same commits any other way skips publishing.

Jobs:
1. publish — checkout at merge_commit_sha, uv + Python 3.13, `uv sync --group dev`, `just lint-all`, `just test-all`, extract the version from the branch name, push tag vX.Y.Z, `uv build`, extract the changelog entry, create the GitHub release with dist/*.whl and dist/*.tar.gz.
2. update-homebrew — needs publish. Download the release wheel, retrying up to five times because the asset takes a moment to appear, compute sha256, checkout oroddlokken/homebrew-tap with secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN, sed the `url` and `sha256` lines in Formula/cboard2.rb, commit and push.

Pin every action by SHA with the version in a trailing comment, as ci.yml already does.

The tag push is the first irreversible step. Any guard belongs before it.

Write Formula/cboard2.rb in oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and wire the token
description:
The tap repo is oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and holds Formula/dogcat.rb and Formula/dogcatwindowbed.rb today. It is a separate repo with no checkout under ~/git — clone it before editing rather than assuming a sibling directory is it.

Model the formula on Formula/dogcat.rb: `include Language::Python::Virtualenv`, url and sha256 pinned to a GitHub release wheel, `depends_on "python@3.13"` (pyproject.toml requires >=3.13), a venv under libexec, and pip-installing the pinned wheel so textual resolves from PyPI.

cboard2 needs no post_install extras — dogcat's exists only for its `[web]` optional group. One entry point, `cboard2` (pyproject.toml:19), so no symlink alias.

`test do system bin/"cboard2", "--help" end`. Confirm cboard2 exits 0 on --help without a TTY before relying on it.

Also add the HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret to the cboard2 repo — a PAT with contents:write on the tap. publish.yml's checkout of the tap fails without it, after the tag has already gone out.

The url and sha256 lines are rewritten by publish.yml on every release, so a hand edit to either is overwritten. Hand edits cover structural changes only: a new runtime dependency, a changed entry point.

description:
publish.yml fires on a merged `release/vX.Y.Z` PR, so a release needs that branch, an RC tag and a PR opened by hand unless a script does it. dogcat's does: /Users/ove/git/dogcat/scripts/release-prep, wired as `just release-prep` and `just next` in its justfile:96-117.

What release-prep does, in order: run lint and tests, stamp CHANGELOG.md with the version, reset an existing `release/v<version>` branch to main (fetching a remote-only one rather than branching off main, which forks a sibling commit no push can fast-forward), force-push with lease, push a `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` tag, open the PR. `just next` reports the candidate patch and minor versions and changes nothing.

cboard2 has no RC release workflow, so decide whether the rc tag stays. It costs nothing and keeps the tag namespace matching dogcat's.

description:
Install today is `uv tool install .` from a clone (README.md:19). The goal is `brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2`, matching how dogcat ships.

dogcat already runs this pipeline end to end, so the work is porting it, not designing it. Read /Users/ove/git/dogcat/docs/releasing.md first, then .github/workflows/publish.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml in that repo.

How dogcat's chain works:
1. A merged PR from a `release/vX.Y.Z` branch fires publish.yml.
2. publish.yml tags vX.Y.Z, runs `uv build`, and creates a GitHub release carrying the wheel and sdist.
3. Its `update-homebrew` job downloads that wheel, computes its sha256, and sed-rewrites `url` and `sha256` in Formula/dogcat.rb in the oroddlokken/homebrew-tap repo, using secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN.
4. The formula (Language::Python::Virtualenv) builds a venv under libexec and pip-installs the pinned wheel.

The formula pins a GitHub release asset, not a PyPI URL, so Homebrew needs no PyPI account.

What cboard2 lacks: LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md, a release workflow, a version derived from git tags (pyproject.toml pins 0.1.0 by hand), a release-prep script, and a Formula/cboard2.rb in the tap. .github/workflows/ holds ci.yml only.

title: Show conflicted, mid-merge and stashed state instead of folding it into dirty
description:
A repo with merge conflicts renders as ordinary dirty work. 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py:279' counts each 'u ' line from 'git status --porcelain=v2' into 'unstaged', so the conflict marker is lost before it reaches a row. Nothing reads '.git/MERGE_HEAD', '.git/rebase-merge' or '.git/rebase-apply' either, so a repo halted mid-rebase looks the same as one with edits in progress. Stashes are not counted at all.

The user opens the dashboard to decide which repo to return to. A conflicted or half-rebased repo needs attention before any other dirty repo, and right now the table cannot say so.

Work: add 'unmerged', 'operation' (none/merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert/bisect) and 'stashed' to RepoState in 'src/cboard2/gitstate.py'; parse 'u ' lines separately in the porcelain reader around line 279; read the in-progress markers from the git dir; count stash entries from 'git stash list' or 'refs/stash'. Render the state in 'src/cboard2/cli.py' state_text and in the TUI table and detail screen in 'src/cboard2/tui.py'. Keep the per-repo cost inside the current poll budget (0.28s for 94 repos at 16 threads) -- prefer a filesystem check over an extra git call.
acceptance: A repo with a conflicted file shows a distinct marker in 'cboard2 ls' and in the dashboard row, not just a raised dirty count. A repo stopped mid-rebase says so. A repo with stashes shows the count. Tests in 'tests/test_gitstate.py' cover a 'u ' status line, each in-progress marker and a non-empty stash.
notes: RepoState gains unmerged, operation and stashed (src/cboard2/gitstate.py). 'u ' lines now count into unmerged instead of unstaged; read_operation() checks rebase-merge/rebase-apply, MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, BISECT_LOG in git's own precedence; count_stashes() reads logs/refs/stash from the common git dir, so a worktree reports its repo's stash. description:
The ahead/behind pair comes from the remote-tracking ref that 'git status --branch' reports, and nothing in a poll fetches -- 'src/cboard2/remote.py:4' states this. The GitHub read in 'remote.py' covers the default branch only: it compares each repo's default-branch tip on GitHub against the local ref. The single fetch in the codebase is 'src/cboard2/pull.py:100', run from shift+P, which targets the default branch.

So a feature branch that gained commits on the remote reports behind=0 forever, and the 'u' (unpushed) filter is the only remote-aware signal a working branch has.

Work: extend the GraphQL query in 'build_query' ('src/cboard2/remote.py:211') to ask for the tip of the checked-out branch per repo alongside the default branch, or add a periodic 'git fetch --prune' on the remote_interval clock for non-dormant repos. Prefer the GraphQL route: it stays hookless and does not write to the repo. Reuse the disk cache in 'src/cboard2/remotecache.py' and the existing 'refresh_local' path so a pull clears the marker on the next poll rather than at the end of the network interval.
acceptance: A repo on a feature branch whose remote gained a commit shows a behind count in 'cboard2 ls --remote' and in the dashboard within one remote interval. A repo on its default branch keeps the behaviour it has today. Tests in 'tests/test_remote.py' cover a non-default branch that is behind, one that is level, and a branch with no remote counterpart.

Conflict test fails in CI: git merge runs without the fixture git identity
description:
tests/test_gitstate.py::test_a_conflict_counts_apart_from_the_ordinary_edits fails on GitHub Actions with 'assert 0 == 1' on state.unmerged (run https://github.com/oroddlokken/cboard2/actions/runs/33975193203/job/101330544540).

Cause: the test calls subprocess.run(["git", "merge", "theirs"], cwd=git_repo, ...) at tests/test_gitstate.py:241 without env. Every other git call goes through the git() helper in tests/conftest.py:63, which passes _GIT_ENV (GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL, GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL). A CI runner has no user.name or user.email in git config, so the merge exits 128 with 'Committer identity unknown' before writing any conflict, leaving unmerged=0. It passes locally only because the developer's ~/.gitconfig supplies an identity.
acceptance: The merge in the test runs with the same env as the git() helper (for example a check=False variant of the helper), and the test fails when run with the git identity stripped from config and env only if the production code is wrong. Verified by running the test with no user.name/user.email available.

publish.yml fires on a merged `release/vX.Y.Z` PR, so a release needs that branch, an RC tag and a PR opened by hand unless a script does it. dogcat's does: /Users/ove/git/dogcat/scripts/release-prep, wired as `just release-prep` and `just next` in its justfile:96-117.

What release-prep does, in order: run lint and tests, stamp CHANGELOG.md with the version, reset an existing `release/v<version>` branch to main (fetching a remote-only one rather than branching off main, which forks a sibling commit no push can fast-forward), force-push with lease, push a `vX.Y.Z-rc.N` tag, open the PR. The tag goes out only after the branch push lands, and a rejected push deletes the local tag and stops — one `push --tags` once published an RC on a commit no branch reached.

`just next` reports the candidate patch and minor versions and changes nothing.

cboard2 has no RC release workflow, so decide whether the rc tag stays. It costs nothing and keeps the tag namespace matching dogcat's.
acceptance:
just next prints the current version and the next patch and minor candidates
just release-prep X.Y.Z opens a release/vX.Y.Z PR with the changelog stamped
release-prep aborts without pushing a tag when the branch push is rejected
notes:
Read of dogcat's source, 2026-09-05:

1. The port must not use a git worktree. dogcat's script builds one (scripts/release-prep:57, :94-129) and removes it in an EXIT trap. This repo's convention forbids worktrees, so the cboard2 version does the branch work in the clone: record the current branch and a clean-tree check up front, check out release/vX.Y.Z, restore the original branch on exit.

2. cboard2 has no CHANGELOG.md, so the stamp step (scripts/release-prep:131-138) has no file to sed. cboard2-4902 adds it; until then either that dependency holds, or the stamp skips when the file is absent.

3. The watch phase (scripts/release-prep:243-299) polls `gh run list -w publish.yml`, which cboard2 lacks until cboard2-4bdn lands. `just next` reads git tags only and works against today's repo.

description:

Add publish.yml: tag, build, GitHub release, tap formula bump
description:
This is the workflow the whole epic hangs on. Port /Users/ove/git/dogcat/.github/workflows/publish.yml, dropping the parts cboard2 has no use for: the pnpm and node steps (cboard2 lints no JS), the publish-pypi job, and the sdist check that only guards PyPI.

Pin every action by SHA with the version in a trailing comment, as ci.yml already does.

The tag push is the first irreversible step. Any guard belongs before it.
acceptance:
Merging a release/vX.Y.Z PR tags vX.Y.Z and creates a GitHub release carrying the wheel
The tap formula's url and sha256 point at that wheel with no hand edit
A merged PR from any other branch name publishes nothing

title: Document the release and swap the README install to brew
Write Formula/cboard2.rb in oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and wire the token
description:
The tap repo is oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and holds Formula/dogcat.rb and Formula/dogcatwindowbed.rb today. It is a separate repo with no checkout under ~/git — clone it before editing rather than assuming a sibling directory is it.

Model the formula on Formula/dogcat.rb: `include Language::Python::Virtualenv`, url and sha256 pinned to a GitHub release wheel, `depends_on "python@3.13"` (pyproject.toml requires >=3.13), a venv under libexec, and pip-installing the pinned wheel so textual resolves from PyPI.

The file stays Formula/cboard2.rb and the class Cboard2, so the install command is `brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2`. The binary it puts on PATH is `cboard` — cboard2-2s4v renames the entry point in pyproject.toml. One entry point, so no symlink alias.

cboard2 needs no post_install extras — dogcat's exists only for its `[web]` optional group.

`test do system bin/"cboard", "--help" end`. Confirm cboard exits 0 on --help without a TTY before relying on it.

Also add the HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret to the cboard2 repo — a PAT with contents:write on the tap. publish.yml's checkout of the tap fails without it, after the tag has already gone out.

The url and sha256 lines are rewritten by publish.yml on every release, so a hand edit to either is overwritten. Hand edits cover structural changes only: a new runtime dependency, a changed entry point.
acceptance:
brew install --build-from-source ./Formula/cboard2.rb succeeds locally and installs bin/cboard
brew test cboard2 passes
The cboard2 repo has a HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN secret with write access to the tap

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Decision 2026-09-05: cut v0.1.0 first, then push the formula with the real url and sha256. The first release's update-homebrew job will fail — Formula/cboard2.rb does not exist for its sed, and HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN is not set on the cboard2 repo (gh secret list returns empty). The release, tag and wheel still land; only the tap bump is missing, and it is filled in by hand once.

Order to follow:
1. User creates a PAT with contents:write on oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and sets it as HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN on oroddlokken/cboard2.
2. User runs just release-prep 0.1.0 and merges the PR.
3. Take the url and sha256 of cboard2-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl from that release, fill them into the formula below, verify brew install --build-from-source and brew test cboard2, then push Formula/cboard2.rb to the tap.

Draft formula (currently at /tmp/hbtap/Formula/cboard2.rb, which does not survive a reboot). desc, homepage and license match pyproject.toml. It pip-installs the pinned wheel into a libexec venv and writes a bin/cboard shim, following Formula/dogcat.rb minus the post_install that only exists for dogcat's [web] extra:

class Cboard2 < Formula
  include Language::Python::Virtualenv

  desc "A terminal dashboard over every git repo on your disk"
  homepage "https://github.com/oroddlokken/cboard2"
  url "https://github.com/oroddlokken/cboard2/releases/download/v0.1.0/cboard2-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
  sha256 "<fill from the release>"
  license "MIT"

  depends_on "python@3.13"

  def install
    venv = virtualenv_create(libexec, "python3.13")
    wheel = "cboard2-#{version}-py3-none-any.whl"
    libexec.install cached_download => wheel
    venv.pip_install libexec/wheel
    (bin/"cboard").write <<~BASH
      #!/bin/bash
      exec "#{libexec}/bin/cboard" "$@"
    BASH
  end

  test do
    system bin/"cboard", "--help"
  end
end

cboard --help exits 0 without a TTY: 'uv run cboard --help | cat' printed 'usage: cboard' and returned 0, so the test do block holds.

release-prep dies when PR checks have not appeared yet
description:
just release-prep 0.1.0 pushed the branch, the RC tag and PR #1, then failed in its watch phase:

  ▸ Waiting for PR checks…
  no checks reported on the 'release/v0.1.0' branch
  ✗ PR checks failed
  error: recipe `release-prep` failed on line 67 with exit code 1

Nothing was lost — the die fires after every push has landed — but the run exits 1, the justfile's following 'git pull origin main' never runs, and the merge wait and publish-workflow wait never start.

Cause: scripts/release-prep:251 runs 'gh pr checks "${BRANCH}" --watch --fail-fast' immediately after 'gh pr create'. GitHub had not registered the PR's ci.yml run yet, and gh exits non-zero for 'no checks reported' exactly as it does for a check that failed. The run appeared 27 seconds later and passed (run 33981117906). cboard2 has no RC release workflow, so the PR's only check comes from ci.yml on the pull_request event, which is what the race is against.

Fix: poll until a check exists, then hand off to --watch --fail-fast. Count them the way the status summary already does, with 'gh pr view "${BRANCH}" --json statusCheckRollup', rather than matching gh's message text. Bound the wait and die with a message that names the empty rollup, so it reads differently from a failed check.

/Users/ove/git/dogcat/scripts/release-prep:251 carries the same line, so a fix here does not propagate there.

Acceptance criteria:
The watch phase waits for the first check to appear instead of dying on an empty rollup
A check that reports failure still exits non-zero with 'PR checks failed'
tests/test_release_prep.py covers a run whose checks appear only after the first poll

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text:
Decision 2026-09-05: cut v0.1.0 first, then push the formula with the real url and sha256. The first release's update-homebrew job will fail — Formula/cboard2.rb does not exist for its sed, and HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN is not set on the cboard2 repo (gh secret list returns empty). The release, tag and wheel still land; only the tap bump is missing, and it is filled in by hand once.

Order to follow:
1. User creates a PAT with contents:write on oroddlokken/homebrew-tap and sets it as HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN on oroddlokken/cboard2.
2. User runs just release-prep 0.1.0 and merges the PR.
3. Take the url and sha256 of cboard2-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl from that release, fill them into the formula below, verify brew install --build-from-source and brew test cboard2, then push Formula/cboard2.rb to the tap.

Draft formula (currently at /tmp/hbtap/Formula/cboard2.rb, which does not survive a reboot). desc, homepage and license match pyproject.toml. It pip-installs the pinned wheel into a libexec venv and writes a bin/cboard shim, following Formula/dogcat.rb minus the post_install that only exists for dogcat's [web] extra:

class Cboard2 < Formula
  include Language::Python::Virtualenv

  desc "A terminal dashboard over every git repo on your disk"
  homepage "https://github.com/oroddlokken/cboard2"
  url "https://github.com/oroddlokken/cboard2/releases/download/v0.1.0/cboard2-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl"
  sha256 "<fill from the release>"
  license "MIT"

  depends_on "python@3.13"

  def install
    venv = virtualenv_create(libexec, "python3.13")
    wheel = "cboard2-#{version}-py3-none-any.whl"
    libexec.install cached_download => wheel
    venv.pip_install libexec/wheel
    (bin/"cboard").write <<~BASH
      #!/bin/bash
      exec "#{libexec}/bin/cboard" "$@"
    BASH
  end

  test do
    system bin/"cboard", "--help"
  end
end

cboard --help exits 0 without a TTY: 'uv run cboard --help | cat' printed 'usage: cboard' and returned 0, so the test do block holds.

Probe tap write access before the tag push in publish.yml
description:
v0.1.1 published, then update-homebrew failed at its push:

  remote: Permission to oroddlokken/homebrew-tap.git denied to oroddlokken.
  fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/oroddlokken/homebrew-tap/': The requested URL returned error: 403

Run 33982401674, job 101349922436. The sed ran and the runner committed 1553c77 locally; only the push was refused, so the tap still points at v0.1.0 while v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 both exist as releases. HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN reads the tap — Checkout homebrew-tap passed — but cannot write it.

The tag push is the first irreversible step, and publish.yml already runs lint, tests and check-sdist ahead of it for that reason. A credential that cannot write the tap is the same class of failure and is not checked at all, so it surfaces only after the tag, the release and the wheel are public.

Add a step to the publish job, before 'Create and push git tag', that probes write access with the endpoint git itself hits:

  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -u "x-access-token:${TAP_TOKEN}" \
    https://github.com/oroddlokken/homebrew-tap.git/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack

200 means the token can push; 403 means it can read only. Do not use GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} and read .permissions.push — that reports the authenticated user's role, and the owner has push whatever the token's own scope is, which is exactly this failure.

The failure message must name the token, the repo and the fix, since whoever reads it is mid-release.

Acceptance criteria:
publish.yml probes tap write access before the tag push and fails there with a message naming HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN
A token with Contents read-only fails the step; one with read and write passes
The token value never reaches the log

title: Probe tap write access before the tag push in publish.yml
Publish cboard2 to Homebrew
description:
Install today is `uv tool install .` from a clone (README.md:19). The goal is `brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2`, matching how dogcat ships.

dogcat already runs this pipeline end to end, so the work is porting it, not designing it. Read /Users/ove/git/dogcat/docs/releasing.md first, then .github/workflows/publish.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml in that repo.

How dogcat's chain works:
1. A merged PR from a `release/vX.Y.Z` branch fires publish.yml.
2. publish.yml tags vX.Y.Z, runs `uv build`, and creates a GitHub release carrying the wheel and sdist.
3. Its `update-homebrew` job downloads that wheel, computes its sha256, and sed-rewrites `url` and `sha256` in Formula/dogcat.rb in the oroddlokken/homebrew-tap repo, using secrets.HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN.
4. The formula (Language::Python::Virtualenv) builds a venv under libexec and pip-installs the pinned wheel.

The formula pins a GitHub release asset, not a PyPI URL, so Homebrew needs no PyPI account.

What cboard2 lacks: LICENSE, CHANGELOG.md, a release workflow, a version derived from git tags (pyproject.toml pins 0.1.0 by hand), a release-prep script, and a Formula/cboard2.rb in the tap. .github/workflows/ holds ci.yml only.
acceptance:
brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2 installs a working cboard on a clean machine
A tagged release updates the tap formula with no hand edit
README.md documents the brew install line
closed_reason: brew install oroddlokken/tap/cboard2 serves 0.1.1; the release wrote the formula's url and sha256 with no hand edit

comments.author: post@rykroken.net
comments.text: PyPI is out of scope: the formula pins a GitHub release wheel, so no publish-pypi job, no scripts/check-sdist and no sdist include-list. License is MIT.
